note: The reviewed delivery and curation every later step changes. Each consumer variable of EXAMPLE is the old `_guarded_ambiguous_lineage` shape: its label '<register> : People' names a source register whose variable is delivered in People and Other (old `second_variant`) and which has a second variant named People (old `duplicate`), and a same_as edge links them, so the build reports one unresolved_lineage_ambiguous_source_variant error per consumer state. EXACT, ORIGINAL, ADDED, CHANGED and LINKED are the old acknowledgement's subject once per drift arm of steps 2 and 3. TWO_ORIGINS is the old earlier-context test: its 2000 state is labelled First origin (FST) and its 2001 state Second origin (SND), each origin linked by same_as. example.toml acknowledges the 2000 issue of every subject, the 2001 TWO_ORIGINS issue stays unacknowledged. Each entry pins both digests. expected_diagnostic_sha256 is the canonical SHA-256 of the issue as the build reports it before acknowledgement, and expected_evidence_sha256 is `lineage_acknowledgement_sha256` over the issue's original records and the complete candidate context the build gathers (consumer, identity-linked candidates of every labelled source, same-named variants, identity edges). Both are copied as a curator copies them; no placeholder renders them, because both need the resolved catalog (precedent: acknowledge-guarded-diagnostic-digest-selects-one-of-two-issues). When the evidence digest narrowed from the whole delivery to each original's own content (maintainer decision 5), each copied evidence pin was rewritten once by the legacy-to-narrowed map that the pre-narrowing code recorded while building this same step (the re-pin tool of that change): a pin is replaced only by the narrowed digest of exactly the inputs whose legacy digest it equalled, so every copy still names step 1's originals and context. Steps 2 and 3 show the copies bind: step 2 (curation changes only) stales exactly the entries it touches, and step 3 shows that a delivery change stales only the entries whose original or candidates changed. From the old tests: an exact entry turns its error into a warning acknowledged by the entry; no lineage edge is written and the ambiguous_source_variant lineage warning is stored; the consumer keeps its literal source text; the acknowledged data warning is published at register level with the entry's reason as its detail.
fails_if: the lineage guard hashes a different context than the curator reviewed (for example `guarded_candidates` keeps only the last labelled source of a subject, or the pipeline passes no `acknowledgement_originals`), so an exact entry goes stale; or `settle_acknowledgements` writes the lineage edge or drops the lineage warning of an acknowledged issue; or `acknowledged_data_warnings` stops publishing the warning of an acknowledged lineage issue
